quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #10
										  					
  

30 Questions • Passing Score 24

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Yield.
Crossroad ahead.
Keep right.
Yield ahead.

questions.explanation: A three-sided sign tells you to slow down and be ready to stop. Yield to other drivers and pedestrians. You can go when it is safe.

questions.question: When is the road most slippery?

options.text: After several hours of rain.
When rain just starts.
After one to two hours of rain.

questions.explanation: Roads are most slippery when rain first begins. Dirt and oil on the road mix with water to create a slick, greasy surface.

questions.question: What is the 'No zone'?

options.text: The blind spots around trucks and buses.
A special speed zone.
A road where car stereos are restricted.
A TV show that replaced The Twilight Zone.

questions.correctAnswerText: The blind spots around trucks and buses.
questions.explanation: Trucks and buses have blind spots on both sides, in back, and in front. Your car cannot be seen in these areas. These spots are called the 'No zone.'

questions.question: Where should you drive when turning left from a two-way street?

options.text: Near the right side of the road.
Near the centerline.
Left of the centerline.

questions.explanation: When turning left from a two-way street, stay in the lane closest to the center. Turn just before your car reaches the center of the intersection. Do not cut the corner. Turn into the first legal lane.

questions.question: Which lane should you be in to turn left from a one-way street?

options.text: The lane nearest the left curb.
The lane nearest the center of the street.
The lane nearest the right curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: The lane nearest the left curb.
questions.explanation: When turning, use the lane closest to where you want to go and turn into the first legal lane. For a left turn from a one-way street, use the lane nearest the left curb.

questions.question: ____ make stopping distances longer and crashes more severe.

options.text: High speeds
Slow speeds
Night drives
Uphill inclines

questions.explanation: High speeds make it take longer to stop and make crashes much worse. The faster you drive, the greater the force when you hit something.

questions.question: Is driving at night more or less dangerous than driving during the day?

options.text: Less dangerous.
No more or less dangerous.
More dangerous.
Easier on your eyes.

questions.explanation: Driving at night is more dangerous. It is harder to see, bright lights from other cars can blind you, and more tired or impaired drivers may be on the road.

questions.question: At a red light with a green arrow, when can you proceed in the direction of the arrow?

options.text: First come to a complete stop.
Wait until the light changes.
You are in the proper lane and the intersection is clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: You are in the proper lane and the intersection is clear.
questions.explanation: You can go in the direction of a green arrow if you are in the proper lane, no matter what other signals show. First, yield to pedestrians and vehicles already in the intersection.

questions.question: What should a driver do?

options.text: Assume all drivers follow right-of-way rules.
Assume most drivers follow right-of-way rules.
Always be ready to give up the right-of-way.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always be ready to give up the right-of-way.
questions.explanation: Do not assume you always have the right-of-way. Watch the situation at every intersection. Give up your right-of-way if it helps prevent a crash.

questions.question: What happens when you take drugs and alcohol together?

options.text: It increases the risk of a crash.
It is no more dangerous than alcohol alone.
It makes alcohol less effective.
It does not affect your driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: It increases the risk of a crash.
questions.explanation: Drugs (prescription, over-the-counter, or illegal) can harm your thinking and make driving unsafe. Mixing drugs with alcohol makes crashes more likely.

questions.question: What does this sign tell you?

options.text: No turns are allowed on this road.
The road narrows ahead.
There are several curves ahead.
The road may be slippery when wet.

questions.explanation: This sign warns drivers about a winding road with three or more curves coming up.

questions.question: When should you allow extra space between your car and the car ahead?

options.text: When following a station wagon.
When following a driver who cannot see the rear of their vehicle.
When following a small passenger car.

questions.correctAnswerText: When following a driver who cannot see the rear of their vehicle.
questions.explanation: Drivers of trucks, buses, vans, and vehicles towing trailers may not see you if you drive directly behind them. Increase your following distance. Large vehicles also block your view of the road ahead, so stay farther back to see around them.

questions.question: What do yellow lines separate?

options.text: Traffic lanes on one-way streets.
Traffic moving in opposite directions on two-way roads.
All carpool lanes from regular traffic lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic moving in opposite directions on two-way roads.
questions.explanation: Yellow lines mark the center of roads with two-way traffic. A solid yellow line means you cannot cross it to pass. A broken yellow line means you can cross it to pass if it is safe.

questions.question: Drivers must always stop for a stopped school bus on a two-lane road.

options.text: TRUE
FALSE

questions.explanation: You must always stop for a stopped school bus on a two-lane road, no matter which direction you are traveling. Always be careful around children.

questions.question: Before turning left, what is most important to do?

options.text: Sound your horn.
Yield to oncoming vehicles.
Swing to the right side of your lane.
Wait until oncoming traffic has a red light.

questions.explanation: When turning left, you must let pedestrians and oncoming traffic pass first.

questions.question: What does a flashing yellow light mean?

options.text: Stop and look, then go if traffic is clear.
Stop and wait for a green light.
Speed up to clear the intersection.
Slow down and proceed with caution.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and proceed with caution.
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means slow down and continue carefully.

questions.question: When turning or stopping in rain, when should you be most careful?

options.text: After it has been raining all day.
One half hour after it stops raining.
During the first half hour of rain.

questions.correctAnswerText: During the first half hour of rain.
questions.explanation: Be extra careful during the first half hour of rain. Oil from cars has not yet washed off the road, creating a slippery mix with the rain.

questions.question: At a railroad crossing, you must:

options.text: Watch for vehicles that must stop at railroad crossings, like school buses and hazmat trucks.
Watch for multiple trains.
Both of the above.

questions.explanation: Approach all railroad crossings with extreme caution. Only cross when you are sure no train is coming from either direction. Also watch for school buses and hazmat trucks that must stop at all railroad crossings.

questions.question: If you see heavy smoke ahead on the road, what should you do?

options.text: Turn on your four-way flashers and keep going.
Slow down, move to the right, and stop off the road.
Turn on high beams and keep going.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down, move to the right, and stop off the road.
questions.explanation: If you see heavy smoke ahead, slow down immediately, drive as far right as possible, and stop off the road. Then decide if it is safe to continue. Some smoke can hurt your eyes and lungs.

questions.question: If your wheels drop off the pavement onto the shoulder, what should you do?

options.text: Brake hard and turn sharply back onto the road.
Stop your car at the edge of the road.
Slow down and carefully turn back onto the road.
Keep your speed and turn sharply back onto the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and carefully turn back onto the road.
questions.explanation: If your wheels drop onto the shoulder, reduce your speed without braking and carefully turn back onto the road. Watch for other traffic when returning to the road.

questions.question: Using a cell phone while driving does not increase your chance of a crash.

options.text: TRUE
FALSE

questions.explanation: Using a phone while driving is a distraction that increases your risk of a crash.

questions.question: A solid white line in the center of a two-lane road means:

options.text: Traffic moves in opposite directions. Drivers cannot pass.
Traffic moves in opposite directions. Drivers can pass when safe.
Traffic moves in the same direction. Drivers cannot pass.
Traffic moves in the same direction. Drivers can pass when safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic moves in the same direction. Drivers cannot pass.
questions.explanation: White lines separate traffic moving in the same direction. A solid white line means drivers cannot pass.

questions.question: At a four-way stop, drivers must yield to all drivers who arrived before them.

options.text: TRUE
FALSE

questions.explanation: At a four-way stop, you must yield to drivers who arrived before you. Wait your turn to enter the intersection.

questions.question: When driving on wet pavement, remember:

options.text: Pavement is extra slippery right when rain starts.
Wet roads can cause hydroplaning.
Give yourself more space when stopping.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Wet roads are slippery, especially when rain first starts. Your vehicle travels on a thin layer of oil, dirt, and water. Slow down in heavy rain, standing water, or slush to prevent your wheels from losing grip.

questions.question: Work zones on highways have become safer for workers and drivers.

options.text: True
False

questions.explanation: Work zones on highways have become more dangerous for both workers and drivers.

questions.question: Double solid yellow lane markings mean:

options.text: Neither lane may pass.
Both lanes may pass.
The right lane may pass.

questions.explanation: Yellow markings separate traffic moving in opposite directions. Double solid yellow lines mean no passing is allowed from either direction.

questions.question: When you see a stop sign, you should stop and:

options.text: Check for vehicles only in the direction you plan to go.
Let all vehicles go first.
Check for traffic in all directions before going.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check for traffic in all directions before going.
questions.explanation: At a stop sign, come to a full stop and check for traffic in all directions before proceeding.

questions.question: If there is no crosswalk and a pedestrian is crossing your lane, you should:

options.text: Make sure the pedestrian can see you before going.
Carefully drive around the pedestrian.
Stop and let the pedestrian finish crossing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and let the pedestrian finish crossing.
questions.explanation: Drivers must always yield to pedestrians in the roadway, even without a marked crosswalk.

questions.question: You may drive around railroad crossing gates:

options.text: When the train has passed.
Never.
When the lights stop flashing.
When other drivers drive around the gates.

questions.explanation: You must stop at all railroad crossings when warned of an approaching train. Warnings include flashing red lights, lowered gates, flaggers, or train signals. Never drive around a lowered gate.

questions.question: Which statement is true?

options.text: Trucks have larger blind spots than cars.
Avoid driving beside a large truck for long periods of time.
Both of the above.

questions.explanation: Trucks have large blind spots behind the cab that extend along the entire truck length. The driver cannot see you, so avoid driving beside or behind large trucks for long periods.
